gallery.title: File:File-Group -Left to Right-- Unidentified 7th Cavalry Trooper, Lieutenant George Armstrong Custer, Dr. Dunbar, Elizabeth Bacon Custer (a4559ee2045c413480ba20840f572e09).tif
gallery.artist: W. J. Phillips (Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument)
gallery.description:
LIBI_00019_00497; This item is an original albumen photograph of a group of 6 people at the headquarters tent at the 7th Cavalry camp near Fort Hayes, Kansas with 4 additional tents and 1 soldier in the background. The photograph is 5 1/2 x 8 1/4" (8" x 9 7/8" mounted).  As noted on page 81 of D. Mark Katz's book, the image was produced in 1869 and is attributable to W.J. Phillips of Preston, Missouri.  The photograph is unevenly cut and has a tear in the upper right corner.  Katz identifies the subjects, from left to right, as: unidentified 7th Cavalry trooper, Lieutenant George A. Custer, Dr. Dunbar, Mrs. Elizabeth B. Custer, Lieutenant Thomas W. Custer, Mrs. A.E. Smith and Mrs. Donald McIntosh.  On the verso, a handwritten notation reads, "Gen'l Custer's headquarters camp/Camp near Ft. Hays Kansas" and is signed by Elizabeth B. Custer.Note: "Pkg #12" handwritten on the verso.Photograph reprinted in "Custer in Photographs" by D. Mark Katz, page 81.; Print, Photographic [Mounted on Card]; Courtesy of the
Keywords: little bighorn battlefield national monument

gallery.title: File:Indian Prision with Wagons and Horse Teams in Front of It, Fort Hays, Kansas (c07a4cab37864d11861590ae85381d8c).tif
gallery.artist: William S. Soule (Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument)
gallery.description:
LIBI_00019_00510; This item is an original albumen, card-mounted photograph of the Indian Prison at Fort Hayes, Kansas with wagons and horse teams in front of the building.  The photograph is 3 x 5 1/4" (4 1/8" x 6 1/4" mounted) and was produced in 1869.  The photographer was possibly W. S. Soule.  The mount, a heavy paper stock, is in poor condition with the upper left corner cut off and torn on the left edge border.  A typed tag is adhered to the front and reads, "Indian Prison, Fort Hayes, Kas. 1869."  A handwritten notation reads, "Property of David [illegible word]."  On the envelope included with this item, a handwritten notation reads, "Indian Prison at Hays" and signed by Elizabeth B. Custer.Note: "Pkg 12/Box 5" handwritten on the envelope.; Print, Photographic [Mounted on Card] Envelope; Courtesy of the National Park Service, Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument, LIBI_00019_00510, William S. Soule, "Indian Prision with Wagons and Horse Teams in Front of It, Fort Hays, Kansas," 1869
Keywords: little bighorn battlefield national monument

gallery.artist: W. J. Phillips (Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument)
gallery.description:
LIBI_00019_00495; This item is an original albumen photograph of a group of 9 people in front General George A. Custer's headquarters at the 7th Cavalry camp near Ft. Hayes, Kansas.  The photograph is 6 x 8 1/8" (8" x 9 7/8" mounted).  As noted on page 83 of D. Mark Katz's book, the image was produced in 1869 and is attributed to W.J. Phillips of Preston, Missouri.  Foxing is evident on the front of the image.  Katz identifies the subjects in the photograph, from left to right, as: Dr. Dunbar, Mrs. Elizabeth B. Custer, Mr. J.R. Young (of the New York Tribune), Captain Thomas B. Weir, Mrs. Nettie Smith, Lieutenant Colonel George A. Custer, Mr. Lamborn (secretary of the Union Pacific Railroad), Mrs. Donald McIntosh and Lieutenant Francis M. Gibson.  On the front, a handwritten notation reads: "A. [illegible word] tent/B. [illegible word] tent/C. [illegible word] tent/[illegible sentence]/Gen'l hdqrs at Ft. Hays 1867-'69/1. Mrs. C./2. Col. Weir/3. Mrs. A.E. Smith/4. [illegible words]/5. [illegible words]/6. [ill
Keywords: little bighorn battlefield national monument
